title: Diagonalizable quotients and the kernel of the character map
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For a finitely generated abelian group $M$ write $D_F(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-group-scheme], where the group algebra has basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$ and Hopf operations $\Delta(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$, $\epsilon(e_m)=1$, $\iota(e_m)=e_{-m}$. Let $M,N$ be finitely generated abelian groups and $\alpha:M\to N$ a homomorphism. Let $f:D_F(N)\to D_F(M)$ be the group-scheme homomorphism induced by $e_m\mapsto e_{\alpha(m)}$. Its fppf sheaf cokernel is canonically $D_F(\ker\alpha)$: the map $D_F(M)\to D_F(\ker\alpha)$ induced by the inclusion $\ker\alpha\subseteq M$ is faithfully flat and has kernel the scheme-theoretic image of $f$. Here an fppf sheaf cokernel is the sheafification of $A\mapsto D_F(M)(A)/f(D_F(N)(A))$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $F$-algebras. Equivalently, if $C\subseteq D_F(M)$ is any closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], then the represented fppf quotient $D_F(M)/C$ [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] is diagonalizable. The groups, subgroups and kernels need not be smooth or reduced, and zero groups are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b),(c), printed pp.233--234, especially the final paragraph of (c) identifying a quotient D(M)/D(M-double-prime) with D(ker(M to M-double-prime)); Definition 12.14, p.236.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker\alpha$ and $L=M/K$. Regard abelian groups as $\mathbf Z$-modules. The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element, since division with remainder leaves a smaller nonnegative element in that ideal; the zero ideal is generated by $0$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applied to $K\subseteq M$ shows that $K$ is finitely generated. The images of generators of $M$ generate $L$, and $L\to N$, $[m]\mapsto\alpha(m)$, is injective by the definition of $K$. By [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria], $D_F(M),D_F(N),D_F(K),D_F(L)$ are affine group schemes of finite type. Their structure maps are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Thus these groups satisfy the finite-type and separatedness hypotheses of the homomorphism theorem used below.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b), pp.233--234: finitely generated groups occurring in the exact sequence; finite generation of subgroups is Stacks Tag 00IK (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-basic).

proof.text: Let $J\subseteq F[M]$ be the ideal generated by $e_k-1$ for $k\in K$. The map $F[M]\to F[L]$, $e_m\mapsto e_{[m]}$, is surjective and has kernel $J$. Indeed, group the finitely many terms of an element by their classes in $L$; its image is zero exactly when the coefficients in each class sum to zero. Choosing a representative $m_0$ for each class appearing in that finite sum writes its contribution as a sum of differences $a_m(e_m-e_{m_0})$. Each such difference lies in $J$, since $e_m-e_{m_0}=e_{m_0}(e_{m-m_0}-1)$. The reverse containment follows by substitution. The map $F[L]\to F[N]$, $e_{[m]}\mapsto e_{\alpha(m)}$, is injective because its basis indices are distinct. Consequently $\ker(f^*)=J$. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $I=D_F(L)\hookrightarrow D_F(M)$ is a closed subgroup through which $f$ factors. It is the scheme-theoretic image: any closed subscheme through which $f$ factors has defining ideal contained in $\ker(f^*)=J$, and hence contains $I$. Write $v:D_F(N)\to I$ for the factor, whose coordinate map is the displayed injection.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b), pp.233--234: augmentation ideal generated by the elements $e_k-1$; the coefficient grouping spells out the displayed quotient-ring identification.

proof.text: Let $q:D_F(M)\to D_F(K)$ be induced by $K\hookrightarrow M$. For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, an $F$-algebra map $F[M]\to A$ is exactly a homomorphism $M\to A^\times$: the images of the $e_m$ are units because $e_me_{-m}=1$, and conversely these images extend uniquely by finite $F$-linear sums. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] these are precisely the $A$-points of $D_F(M)$. Under this description $q$ is restriction to $K$. Its kernel consists of the homomorphisms trivial on $K$, which factor uniquely through $L=M/K$. Thus $\ker q=I=D_F(L)$ as subgroup functors, with the inclusion already constructed in step 2. This is a scheme-theoretic kernel, since the same formula holds for every algebra $A$, including algebras with nilpotents.

Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] separately to $q:D_F(M)\to D_F(K)$ and to $v:D_F(N)\to D_F(L)$. All four groups meet its hypotheses by step 1. Each factors as a faithfully flat finitely presented homomorphism followed by a closed immersion. Each closed intermediate scheme is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On coordinate algebras the closed-immersion map is surjective and its composite with the other map is injective: for $q$ this composite sends the distinct basis elements $e_k$ to the same indexed elements in $F[M]$; for $v$ it is the injection from step 2. Therefore the surjection is also injective and is an algebra isomorphism. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] each closed factor is an isomorphism of schemes. It follows that $q$ and $v$ themselves are faithfully flat and finitely presented. The same factorization theorem identifies $D_F(K)$ with the represented fppf quotient $D_F(M)/I$, compatibly with $q$, since step 3 computed its kernel as $I$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b), p.233, using Proposition 5.43(c) => (a), p.109, and Theorem 5.39, p.108; the quotient-sheaf interpretation is Section 5(j), pp.116--118.

proof.text: The cokernel sheaf of $f$ equals the quotient sheaf by $I$. To check this directly on the specified coset presheaves, use the map $D_F(M)(A)/f(D_F(N)(A))\to D_F(M)(A)/I(A)$. It is surjective. If two classes have the same image, their difference is represented by an element of $I(A)$. Since $v$ is an fppf quotient map by step 4 and [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization], that element is in $v(D_F(N)(A'))$ on an fppf covering $A\to A'$; the two classes therefore become equal on that covering. Thus the two presheaves have the same sheafification: local representatives lift and any two lifts agree locally, so they glue uniquely in every sheaf receiving such representatives. Represented functors are sheaves for these coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Step 4 now gives the canonical cokernel $D_F(K)$, with cokernel map exactly $q$. Together with steps 2--3 this proves the first assertion, including the specified scheme-theoretic image and faithful flatness.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b),(c), pp.233--234, and Section 5(j), pp.116--118; representable descent is Stacks Tags 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), 03O3 (etale-cohomology-lemma-representable-sheaf-fpqc).

proof.text: Now let $C\subseteq D_F(M)$ be any closed subgroup. Choose finitely many generators of $M$, giving a surjection $\mathbf Z^r\to M$ for some $r\geq0$. Its induced coordinate map $F[\mathbf Z^r]\to F[M]$ is surjective, so [def-weil-closed-immersion] embeds $D_F(M)$ into $D_F(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, where the isomorphism is [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria]. The composite embedding of $C$ is also closed: on these affine schemes its coordinate map is a composite of two surjections. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable] to this closed subgroup of $\mathbf G_m^r$. It gives an isomorphism $C\simeq D_F(P)$ for a finitely generated abelian group $P$. No smoothness or reducedness is needed at this step.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(c), p.234 (closed subgroups), and Definition 12.14, p.236 (diagonalizable groups as subgroups of split tori).

proof.text: Over the algebraically closed field $F$, the split character antiduality of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] identifies the inclusion $D_F(P)\simeq C\hookrightarrow D_F(M)$ with the morphism induced by a surjection $\beta:M\to P$: its character groups identify with $P$ and $M$, and a closed immersion induces a surjection on characters. Apply the result already proved in steps 1--5 to this concrete $\beta$. Its image is exactly $C$, so its fppf cokernel is $D_F(\ker\beta)$. The subgroup $C$ is normal because $D_F(M)$ is commutative on every algebra, so this cokernel agrees with the represented fppf quotient of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Hence $D_F(M)/C$ is diagonalizable. All computations used group-algebra bases or points over arbitrary algebras; none removed nilpotents. If one of the groups is zero, its group algebra is $F$ and the same maps and computations apply unchanged.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(c), final paragraph, p.234: identify the subgroup with $D(M^{\prime\prime})$ and take $\ker(M\to M^{\prime\prime})$.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 12.9(b),(c), printed pp.233--234, with the affine homomorphism theorem (5.39), injective-coordinate criterion (5.43), and quotient-sheaf interpretation (5(j)); the group-algebra kernel calculation is written explicitly.
